newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Rioting Bangladesh prisoners make their demand.
newsitem.headline: Rioting Bangladesh prisoners make their demand.

text.p: A Bangladesh prison revolt stretched into its third day on Wednesday with inmates in control of the complex demanding to meet Home (interior) Minister Rafiqul Islam, police said.
The prisoners, angered by being left out of an independence day amnesty, took over Jessore jail on Monday after scaring away guards with iron bars and knives.
Police said the situation was tense and officials at the jail, 270 km (160 miles) west of the capital Dhaka, said they were worried about the fate of 300 female prisoners.
"We are trying to settle the crisis without applying any force. We are continuing our negotiations," a police official contacted by telephone told Reuters.
The trouble started after 90 prisoners were freed nationwide under an amnesty awarded as part of Monday's 25th independence anniversary celebrations.
The prison holds about 3,000 prisoners, some convicts and others on remand. Some were demanding freedom while others sought better food and treatment.
On Wednesday, senior police officials, aided by local political and community leaders, were trying to establish contact with the prisoners with loudspeakers.
"They (prisoners) want (the) home minister to come and assure them of meeting their demands. Otherwise, they threatened to continue their siege," a police official said.
Jail officials said the prison had food stocks for two weeks.
The authorities brought in more riot police and para-military troops from nearby districts to prevent breakout attempts.
"We are very anxious about the safety of about the female prisoners," said one jail official.
